correctness.rationale: For N=product p_i^{e_i}, D(N) is order-isomorphic to a product of chains [0,e_i], graded by rho=sum coordinates, top rank S=sum e_i. With two reusable symbols define H_0(z)=true and H_{j+1}(z)=exists w(w<z and H_j(w)), where w alternates symbols and nested shadowing is legal. H_j exactly asserts rho>=j; hence exact rank and S are FO²-visible. When at least two factors, for atom a_i the maximum rank of an element incomparable with it is S-e_i, so an FO² unary formula identifies atoms of each exponent e. A two-symbol sentence Psi_{S,e,k} asks whether a rank-k element dominates every such atom; its least successful k is exactly the number m_e of factors of exponent e. Thus all exponent multiplicities are reconstructed without counting, for any r. Chains r=1 are distinguished by comparability and recovered height; N=1 by rank zero. Conversely equal exponent multisets give isomorphic products. In FO¹ only equality and reflexivity are atomic, so all these nonempty posets satisfy the same FO¹ sentences. The proof uses unbounded quantifier rank and is RELATIVE to finite divisor lattices, not absolute FO² finite-poset categoricity.

originality.rationale: Products-of-chains descriptions are classical. Kiefer–Schweitzer–Selman study identification by TWO-VARIABLE WITH COUNTING (stronger logic, broader structure domain); Zeume–Harwath study order invariance with named linear orders; Marzec–Tendera study satisfiability of two-variable logics with partial-order relations. None of the inspected theorem statements directly gives the counting-free relative identification of prime-exponent multisets by pure divisibility. This may be an implicit known property of finite distributive lattices and is a qualified best-of-knowledge original finding.
residual_risks: A classical finite distributive-lattice FO² characterization might already imply the divisor-lattice special case.
No claim of FO² categoricity among ALL finite posets; unbounded quantifier rank is essential.

value.rationale: Recovering complete prime-exponent multiplicities from a language with no counting and only two reusable variable names is a natural expressive-power rigidity question. It gives a strong relative identification theorem for all finite divisor lattices, with a sharp one-versus-two-variable threshold, rather than just an example or another product-of-chains isomorphism classification.
